OncallBot: :rotating_light: Incident detected — high rate of container restarts on gpu-serving-prod-3s in cluster: inference-prod (alert: prefill_gpu_oom_count > 5 in 2m)
Alex: seeing multiple containers entering CrashLoopBackOff, logs show CUDA OOM during prefill for requests with long context (>120k tokens). attaching sample stack: `RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory during prefill`
Maria: confirmed customer reports of degraded completions for two large customers on us-west. latency spikes and ~30% error rate for large-context models.
Jordan: can we switch those routes to the smaller quantized variant to buy time? route map shows model-llama-70b-fp16 and model-llama-70b-q4 are compatible with fallback.
SRE: starting immediate mitigations: 1) cordon & drain suspect node(s) 2) scale up dedicated pool with spare gpus 3) enable model fallback for affected routes. executing now.
Alex: dump from pod (gpu-serving-prod-3s-77):
```
[2026-03-17T02:15:41Z] prefill buffer allocate 13.2GB
[2026-03-17T02:15:41Z] Realloc failed -> CUDA OOM
[2026-03-17T02:15:41Z] Container restarted (exit code 137)
```
Maria: customer-impact summary for pager: two enterprise tenants experienced latency > 10s and ~25% failed requests in the 02:10–02:25 window. no data exfiltration, only availability.
Jordan: routing change pushed: `/v1/completions/large-context` now pinned to model-llama-70b-q4 on us-west and eu-west. watch logs for degraded quality complaints.
Mike: I toggled `prefill_kv_cache_limit` down from 1.0 -> 0.6 for the affected model to reduce memory pressure. patch applied to live config via console.
SRE: scaled up GPU pool by 2 nodes (g5xlarge-equivalent). autoscaler triggered extra pods. evicting long-running prefills via `/ops/evict-long-prefill` job.
Alex: still seeing a small number of restarts pinned to one node (inference-prod-node-7). drainer reports kernel messages: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79` — possible driver-level reset.
Maria: raising severity to P1 for customer-impacting degradation. notifying support to prepare customer messages.
Jordan: oncall runbook checklist (quick):
- confirm impacted routes and customers
- enable model fallback -> done
- reduce prefill limits and cache sizes -> done
- cordon & drain faulty node -> in progress
- scale up pool -> done
- open bridge + handoff note for next rotation -> pending
SRE: drainer completed, node shows repeated driver resets. isolating node and scheduling hardware replacement with cloud provider.
Mike: starting canary verification: 10% of traffic to fallback model, monitoring prompt quality metrics and latency.
Alex: logs look stable post-fallback, error rate down from 25% to ~3% in last 5m. but one job still flapping due to a very long single prefill request (customer A) — I reached out to their SE to ask for rate-limiting/shorter window.
Maria: drafting customer-facing note: short outage for large-context requests, mitigation in place, working on permanent fix (driver, memory accounting, and prefill throttling).
OncallBot: Bridge created: https://company-bridges/4220003141, pager duty rotation oncall: @Alex -> next oncall @Jordan in 4h.
Jordan: I'll take over the postmortem and remediation actions: (1) add automatic fallback policy for oversized prefill requests, (2) improve prefill memory accounting to fail early, (3) add driver-reset detection to alert before crash.
SRE: leaving a final note in runbook: ensure node replacement ticket created (cloud-ticket-99831) and schedule follow-up with infra team.
Mike: handoff status: all mitigations applied, traffic stabilized, monitoring zoom link pinned. handing to @Jordan for next 4h. :white_check_mark:
Jordan: acknowledged, will run through the runbook and post a summary after warm-up window.
